newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade lawyers to protest over high taxes.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade lawyers to protest over high taxes.

text.p: Belgrade lawyers said on Wednesday they would walk out of the city's courts this week in protest at high taxes they say are driving them into poverty.
"Belgrade lawyers will try to exert pressure on the authorities by blocking the courts for a week," Radoslav Nedic, president of the the Belgrade Bar Association told Reuters.
The Bar Association met on Monday and decided to launch a seven-day protest from November 15.
Nedic said the action was a protest and not a strike, as Serbian law prohibits laywers from striking.
He said lawyers wanting to take home the statistical average of 1,180 dinars ($236) a month must make at least three times that amount before tax. They demanded an overhaul of the tax system.
A similar protest in the last week of October leading up to Yugoslavia's November 3 elections blocked Belgrade's courts for three days without yielding results.
